name: Bluebell
overview: Bluebell is the first free route up the North Norwegian Buttress of Mount Index: about 2,000 ft of climbing graded 5.13-, protected entirely by bolts, with roughly a third of its pitches overhanging. Most of it is sustained 5.11-5.12. It is its own line, independent of the Doorish, Voodoo Project and Jötnar aid routes, and it took more than 25 days on the wall to establish in 2023.
beta: Seventeen pitches as usually linked (21 if split at every stance), in six sections: the Toe (P1-3); the slightly overhanging Shield (P4-6) with the 3D Dike and a boulder-problem crux on blank pinches; the steep Roofs (P7-8); the technical Slab (P9-11), with a ledge at P10 that takes a portaledge; the overhanging Headwall (P12-15) with the 5.13- crux; and easier, barely cleaned Summit pitches (P16-17). Bring a stick clip for the headwall bolts.
descent_text: Bluebell is descended by rappelling the route, not by a walk-off. Every belay is bolted and rigged for rappel, and the whole 2,000 ft can be rappelled on a single, uncut 70 m rope; an 80 m rope gives more flexibility. Dedicated rappel anchors set off the climbing line let you skip some belays and avoid the overhanging headwall pitches, which would otherwise leave you hanging in space. From the base, reverse the talus traverse around Lake Serene to the maintained trail.
descent: Rappel the route on a single 70 m rope; every anchor is rigged for rappel, and dedicated rappel anchors let the descent skip belays, including the overhanging headwall ones.
rappels: Single 70m rope; every belay is bolted and rap-equipped, with dedicated rap-line anchors that let parties skip some belays for a faster single-rope descent, especially through the Headwall.

pitch_detail.notes: Mostly high-quality, less-than-vertical rock, with some scrambling along ledges.
Slightly overhanging, easing toward vertical; includes the 3D Dike and a boulder-problem crux (about V7) on blank pinches.
Steep, three-dimensional climbing on underclings and jugs, with a key pinch through the roof.
Technical face climbing on excellent stone; the ledge at P10 takes a portaledge.
Overhanging for all four pitches, with boulder-problem cruxes (about V6 and V5); stick-clip some bolts.
Minimally cleaned mountain climbing; loose rock on the ledges near the top.

fa: Nathan Hadley, Michal Rynkiewicz and Stamati Anagnostou, 2023. First free ascent: Hadley, August 11, 2023, with Luke Stefurak; Rynkiewicz and Anagnostou freed it August 21-22, 2023.
